about: Batch 04, slice A, chunk A39: lunches from West, East and Southern Africa, Latin American plates (bandeja, casado, prato feito, pabellon) and Hawaiian and Pacific plate lunches.

recipes.title: Suya Chicken Wraps (Nigerian Peanut-Spiced Chicken)
recipes.summary: Quick-seared chicken rubbed with a peanut and chilli spice mix, rolled with tomato, onion and cabbage.
steps: Mix the peanut, chilli powder, paprika, ginger, garlic powder and salt, and toss the chicken through it.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat and cook the chicken for 6 to 8 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through to 75°C.
Warm the tortillas, fill with the chicken, tomato, onion and cabbage, and roll up.
notes: Food safety: chicken must be cooked through to 75°C with no pink. Pack chilled with an ice pack if taking it to work and eat within 4 hours.
Contains peanut and gluten.

recipes.title: Jollof Rice Bowl with Fried Plantain and Egg
recipes.summary: Tomato and capsicum jollof rice with golden plantain and a fried egg on top.
steps: Soften the onion and capsicum in the first measure of oil for 5 minutes, then stir in the tomato paste, curry powder and thyme for 2 minutes.
Add the tinned tomatoes, stock, salt and rice, cover and simmer on low for 20 minutes, until the rice is tender and the liquid has been absorbed.
Fry the plantain in the second measure of oil for 3 minutes each side until golden, then set aside and fry the eggs in the same pan.
Serve the rice topped with plantain and an egg.
notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set. Cool leftover rice within an hour and eat within 1 day, reheated until steaming hot.
Contains egg.

recipes.title: Red Red (Ghanaian Black-Eyed Bean Stew with Plantain)
recipes.summary: Spiced tomato and black-eyed bean stew with fried sweet plantain, a vegan Ghanaian favourite.
steps: Soften the onion, garlic, ginger and chilli in the first measure of oil for 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and paste and cook for 5 minutes, then stir in the beans, water and salt and simmer for 12 minutes.
Fry the plantain in the second measure of oil for 3 minutes each side until golden.
Serve the stew with the plantain alongside.
notes: Wash your hands after handling the scotch bonnet and leave the seeds out for less heat.

recipes.title: Fataya (Senegalese Tuna Pastries)
recipes.summary: Crisp baked filo parcels filled with spiced tuna and onion, a Dakar street lunch.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C. Soften the onion in the first measure of oil for 5 minutes, add the mustard seed, chilli, cumin and salt, then fold in the tuna and parsley and cool for 5 minutes.
Cut each filo sheet in half lengthways, brush with oil and fold into 6 triangle parcels around spoonfuls of the filling.
Brush the tops with the remaining oil and bake for 15 minutes until golden and crisp.
notes: Food safety: keep tinned tuna chilled once opened. Cool the parcels within an hour; eat within 2 days and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains fish and gluten.

recipes.title: Misir Wot Flatbread Plate (Ethiopian Spiced Red Lentils)
recipes.summary: Slow-simmered red lentils in a deep berbere-style spice blend, scooped up with warm flatbread.
steps: Cook the onion in the oil over medium heat for 8 minutes, then add the garlic, ginger, paste and spices and stir for 2 minutes.
Add the lentils, water and salt, simmer for 15 minutes, stirring often, until thick and soft.
Warm the flatbread and serve with the lentils.
notes: Contains gluten.

recipes.title: Atkilt Wat (Ethiopian Cabbage, Potato and Chickpea Plate)
recipes.summary: Turmeric-gold cabbage, potato and carrot stew with chickpeas, mild and filling.
steps: Cook the onion in the oil for 6 minutes, add the garlic, ginger and turmeric for 1 minute.
Add the potato, carrot and water, cover and simmer for 10 minutes, then add the cabbage, chickpeas and salt and cook 8 minutes more until tender.
Serve warm in bowls, with a squeeze of lemon if you like.
notes: Good cold the next day as a packed lunch.

recipes.title: Githeri (Kenyan Maize and Bean Bowl with Avocado)
recipes.summary: Kenyan maize and kidney beans fried with tomato and onion, topped with creamy avocado.
steps: Soften the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, add the tomatoes and turmeric and cook for 4 minutes.
Stir in the beans, corn, salt and water and simmer for 8 minutes until the liquid has reduced.
Serve topped with avocado and coriander.
notes: Make a double batch; it reheats well.

recipes.title: Sukuma Wiki with Fried Eggs and Polenta
recipes.summary: Garlicky Kenyan braised kale with tomato and onion, a fried egg and a wedge of firm polenta in place of ugali.
steps: Whisk the polenta into the boiling salted water and stir over low heat for 8 minutes until thick, then spread into a dish to firm.
Cook the onion in the first measure of oil for 5 minutes, add the garlic and tomatoes for 3 minutes, then the kale and 3 tbsp water, covered, for 6 minutes.
Fry the eggs in the second measure of oil until the whites are set, cut the polenta into wedges and serve with the kale and eggs.
notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set.
Contains egg.

recipes.title: Vegetarian Bunny Chow (South African Curry Beans in Bread)
recipes.summary: A Durban classic: hollowed bread loaf filled with a spiced bean and potato curry.

items: 1 crusty bread, cut into 2 lengths, hollowed

steps: Soften the onion, garlic and ginger in the oil for 5 minutes, stir in the curry powder for 1 minute.
Add the tomato, potato, water and salt, simmer for 12 minutes, then add the beans and cook 4 minutes until thick.
Spoon the curry into the hollowed bread, top with coriander and serve with the bread lids on the side.
notes: Contains gluten.

recipes.title: Boerewors-Style Sausage Rolls with Tomato Relish
recipes.summary: Grilled spiced pork sausage in a soft roll with a quick tomato and onion relish, South African braai style.
steps: Cook the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, add the tomatoes, sugar, vinegar and salt and simmer for 10 minutes into a thick relish.
Rub the sausages with the coriander and pepper, then grill or pan-fry over medium heat for 12 to 15 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through to 75°C.
Tuck the sausages into the buns and top with the relish.
notes: Food safety: pork sausages must be cooked through to 75°C with no pink. Eat packed lunches within 4 hours, chilled, and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten.

recipes.title: Gatsby (Cape Town Steak and Chips Roll)
recipes.summary: A long roll stuffed with seared steak strips, hot chips, onion and sauce, a Cape Town sharing classic.
steps: Bake the chips as the pack directs, about 20 minutes.
Season the steak with paprika, garlic powder and a pinch of salt. Cook with the onion in the oil over high heat for 4 minutes until browned and cooked through (63°C or more).
Spread mayonnaise and tomato sauce in the rolls, fill with the chips, steak, onion and tomato.
notes: Food safety: beef steak cooked to at least 63°C. Pack chilled and eat within 4 hours.
Contains egg and gluten.

recipes.title: Chakalaka Beans on Toast with Fried Egg
recipes.summary: Baked beans lifted with carrot, capsicum and curry spice in a quick chakalaka, piled on toast with an egg.
steps: Soften the onion, carrot and capsicum in the oil for 6 minutes, stir in the curry powder, then add the tomato and beans and simmer for 6 minutes.
Fry the eggs until the whites are set.
Cook the eggs until the whites are set, then pile the beans on the toast and top with an egg and parsley.
notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set.
Contains egg and gluten.

recipes.title: Bandeja Paisa Lunch Plate (Colombian Rice, Beans, Chorizo and Egg)
recipes.summary: A trimmed-down Colombian platter of rice, red beans, chorizo, plantain, avocado and a fried egg.
steps: Cook the rice in 280 ml salted water, covered, for 15 minutes. Simmer the beans with the tomato, spring onion, cumin and 100 ml water for 12 minutes until thick.
Fry the chorizo in a dry pan for 4 minutes, remove, and fry the plantain in the oil for 3 minutes each side. Fry the eggs in the same pan until the whites are set.
Plate the rice with beans, chorizo, plantain, egg and avocado.
notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set and the chorizo until hot through to 75°C.
Contains egg.

recipes.title: Casado (Costa Rican Chicken, Rice and Black Bean Plate)
recipes.summary: The classic Costa Rican set lunch: seared chicken, rice, black beans, fried plantain and a lime cabbage slaw.
steps: Cook the rice in the water with a pinch of salt, covered, for 15 minutes. Warm the beans with 50 ml water.
Season the chicken with cumin and salt and cook in the first measure of oil for 6 minutes each side until cooked through to 75°C. Rest 3 minutes, then slice.
Fry the plantain in the second measure of oil for 3 minutes each side. Toss the cabbage with the lime juice and coriander.
Plate everything together.
notes: Food safety: chicken must be cooked through to 75°C with no pink.

recipes.title: Prato Feito (Brazilian Steak, Egg, Rice and Beans Plate)
recipes.summary: The everyday Brazilian lunch plate: seared steak, fried egg, rice, stewed beans and tomato.
steps: Cook the rice in the water, covered, for 15 minutes. Soften the garlic in 1 tbsp of the oil, add the beans and 100 ml water and simmer for 10 minutes.
Season the steak with salt and sear in a hot pan for 3 to 4 minutes each side, rest for 4 minutes and slice. Fry the eggs in the remaining oil until the whites are set.
Toss the tomato and onion with the lime juice and plate everything together.
notes: Food safety: cook steak to at least 63°C and rest it. Cook the eggs until the whites are set.
Contains egg.

recipes.title: Gallo Pinto Bowl with Fried Egg and Avocado (Costa Rican Rice and Beans)
recipes.summary: Rice and black beans fried with onion, capsicum and a splash of Worcestershire, topped with egg and avocado.
steps: Cook the rice in the water with a pinch of salt, covered, for 15 minutes.
Soften the onion and capsicum in the first measure of oil for 5 minutes, add the beans, cumin and Worcestershire sauce and the rice, and stir-fry for 5 minutes until hot and lightly speckled.
Fry the eggs in the second measure of oil until the whites are set.
Serve the rice topped with egg, avocado and coriander.
notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set. Cool leftover rice within an hour and eat within 1 day.
Contains egg and fish (Worcestershire sauce).

recipes.title: Sanguche de Pollo (Peruvian Chicken Sandwich with Aji Cream)
recipes.summary: Warm sliced chicken in a crusty roll with creamy jalapeño and lime sauce and red onion.
steps: Season the chicken with cumin and salt, cook in the oil for 5 to 6 minutes each side until cooked through to 75°C, then rest 3 minutes and slice.
Mix the mayonnaise, jalapeño and half the lime juice. Toss the onion in the rest of the juice.
Fill the rolls with lettuce, chicken, onion and the cream.
notes: Food safety: chicken must be cooked through to 75°C with no pink. Pack chilled and eat within 4 hours.
Contains egg and gluten.

recipes.title: Patacones with Fried Egg and Avocado (Ecuadorian Twice-Fried Plantain)
recipes.summary: Crisp smashed green plantain discs topped with a runny egg, avocado and fresh salsa.

items: 2 plantain, peeled and cut in thick rounds

steps: Fry the plantain rounds in 2 tbsp oil for 3 minutes each side, then smash flat between baking paper and fry again for 2 minutes each side until crisp. Sprinkle with salt.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil until the whites are set.
Mix the tomato, onion and lime juice. Top the patacones with eggs, avocado and salsa.
notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set.
Contains egg.

recipes.title: Loco Moco (Hawaiian Beef Patty, Egg and Gravy Rice Bowl)
recipes.summary: A Hawaiian diner staple: rice topped with a juicy beef patty, fried egg and rich onion gravy.
steps: Cook the rice in 320 ml water, covered, for 15 minutes. Shape the mince with salt and pepper into 2 patties.

Cook the patties in a pan over medium-high heat for 5 minutes each side until cooked through to 75°C, then set aside. Cook the onion in the same pan for 5 minutes, stir in the flour, then add the stock and soy sauce and simmer 4 minutes into a gravy.
Fry the eggs until the whites are set, then stack rice, patty, egg and gravy in bowls and top with spring onion.
notes: Food safety: beef patties must be cooked through to 75°C with no pink. Cook the eggs until the whites are set.
Contains egg and gluten.

recipes.title: Hawaiian Garlic Prawn Plate Lunch with Rice and Pineapple
recipes.summary: North Shore style garlic butter prawns with steamed rice and sweet pineapple.
steps: Cook the rice in 320 ml water, covered, for 15 minutes.
Melt the butter over medium heat and cook the garlic and paprika for 1 minute, then add the prawns and salt and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until pink and curled. Add the lemon juice.
Serve over rice with pineapple and parsley.
notes: Food safety: prawns must be opaque and pink all the way through. Eat leftovers within 1 day, reheated until steaming hot.
Contains crustacean shellfish and milk.

recipes.title: Huli Huli Chicken Plate with Rice and Slaw
recipes.summary: Pineapple, soy and ginger glazed chicken thighs with rice and a crunchy cabbage slaw.
steps: Cook the rice in 320 ml water, covered, for 15 minutes. Mix the soy, sugar, juice, ginger and garlic.
Brown the chicken in the oil for 5 minutes each side, pour in the sauce and cook for 6 minutes, turning, until glossy and cooked through to 75°C.
Toss the cabbage and carrot with the vinegar. Sear the pineapple rings in the pan until caramelised and serve everything together.
notes: Food safety: chicken must be cooked through to 75°C with no pink.
Contains soy.

recipes.title: Pacific Corned Beef and Coconut Spinach Rice
recipes.summary: Tinned corned beef fried with onion and folded through coconut spinach rice, a Pacific island pantry lunch.
steps: Cook the rice with the coconut milk, water and salt, covered, on low for 15 minutes.
Fry the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, add the corned beef and cook for 4 minutes until crisp at the edges.
Fold the spinach and corned beef through the hot rice, cover for 2 minutes and finish with lime.
notes: Food safety: keep opened tinned corned beef chilled and use within 2 days.

recipes.title: Sapasui (Samoan Glass Noodle Stir-Fry)
recipes.summary: Soy and ginger glass noodles tossed with beef, carrot and cabbage, a Samoan potluck favourite.
steps: Soak the noodles in hot water for 8 minutes, drain and snip into shorter lengths.
Stir-fry the beef in the oil over high heat for 3 minutes, add the onion, garlic, ginger and carrot for 3 minutes.
Add the cabbage, soy, water and noodles and toss for 3 minutes until the liquid is absorbed.
notes: Food safety: cook the beef until browned and cooked through to at least 63°C.
Contains soy.

recipes.title: Dibi Lamb Baguette (Senegalese Grilled Lamb with Onion Mustard)
recipes.summary: Grilled lamb strips in a crusty baguette with a hot mustard and caramelised onion sauce, Dakar roadside style.
steps: Season the lamb with pepper, garlic powder and salt and cook in half the oil over high heat for 5 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through to 63°C. Set aside.
Cook the onions in the rest of the oil for 12 minutes until soft and golden, then stir in the mustard and vinegar.
Fill the baguette with the lamb and onion mustard.
notes: Food safety: lamb must be cooked to at least 63°C. Pack chilled and eat within 4 hours.
Contains gluten and mustard.

recipes.title: Kelewele Plantain and Peanut Wraps (Ghanaian Spiced Fried Plantain)
recipes.summary: Ginger and chilli spiced plantain cubes fried until caramelised, wrapped with peanuts, tomato and cabbage.
steps: Toss the plantain with the ginger, cayenne and salt.
Fry in the oil over medium-high heat for 8 minutes, turning, until deep golden and caramelised at the edges.
Warm the flatbread, fill with plantain, peanuts, tomato and cabbage, and squeeze over the lime.
notes: Contains peanut and gluten.
